title: Usage Addition Tiers, Restored Dual-Fuel Credits on Residential Electricity Supply
content:
A restored dual-fuel credit on a Residential Electricity Supply agreement carries a usage addition decided by the agreement's recent average consumption.

**Average consumption.** The kWh on the agreement's energy charge lines whose billing cycle started less than twelve whole months before the restoration date are added up and divided by the number of those energy charge lines. On a time-of-use agreement the on-peak and off-peak lines are each one line. An agreement with no such lines receives nothing.

**Tiers.**

| Average kWh per energy charge line | Usage addition |
|---|---|
| 1,000 kWh or more | 1.00 USD (high-usage addition) |
| from 800 up to but not including 1,000 kWh | 0.50 USD (mid-usage addition) |
| below 800 kWh | nothing |

**Boundaries.** An average of exactly 1,000 kWh earns 1.00 USD and 999.9 kWh earns 0.50 USD; an average of exactly 800 kWh earns 0.50 USD and 799.9 kWh earns nothing.

**Example (hypothetical).** Twelve flat-rate energy lines in the window total 10,200 kWh: the average is 850 kWh and the usage addition is 0.50 USD. Had they totalled 12,000 kWh, the average would be 1,000 kWh and the addition 1.00 USD.
